macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Fed holds rates steady as markets await Powell remarks
items.summary: The Federal Reserve left the policy rate unchanged at 5.25%–5.50%, matching expectations, and markets were focused on Chair Jerome Powell's press conference. Newsquawk also reported that S&P futures were down 0.4% and Nasdaq futures were down 0.6% around the announcement.

items.title: Swiss National Bank keeps interest rate at 0.00%
items.summary: The Swiss National Bank left its policy rate unchanged at 0.00% and said it is willing to be active in foreign exchange markets as necessary to ensure appropriate monetary conditions. The decision adds to the day's central-bank focus across developed markets.

items.title: U.S. mortgage rates rise above 7% for first time since January 2025
items.summary: Freddie Mac said the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 7.03% from 6.95% the prior week, the highest since January 2025. The move underscores persistent affordability pressure in the housing market.

items.title: Wall Street mixed as bond yields rise and oil cools
items.summary: AP reported that the S&P 500 ended the week virtually unchanged, the Dow rose, and the Nasdaq fell as rising bond yields drove volatility. The S&P 500 remained near its all-time high despite the swings.

items.title: U.S. yields stay elevated as investors watch inflation and growth data
items.summary: Market coverage cited U.S. 10-year Treasury yields touching 5.23% during the week before finishing at 5.17%, while the 30-year yield reached 5.53%, the highest since 2004. The moves reflect continuing pressure from strong economic data and elevated inflation expectations.

items.title: Fed officials signal persistent inflation concerns
items.summary: Recent remarks from Fed officials including Beth Hammack emphasized that high inflation remains a challenge for economic planning, reinforcing the market's focus on the central bank's hawkish tone. Separate reporting said traders were pricing in a meaningful chance of another rate hike later this year.

items.title: Wall Street finishes the week higher despite yield volatility
items.summary: Reuters-sourced coverage in AP and other wire reports said the major U.S. indexes ended the week higher overall, with the S&P 500 up 1.21%, the Nasdaq up 2.06%, and the Dow up 0.28%. The gains came even as bond-market turbulence dominated sentiment.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $84,000 as yields pressure crypto despite regulatory progress
items.summary: Bitcoin was trading around $84,000 after a modest decline, with rising U.S. Treasury yields weighing on risk assets. The report also noted mixed regulatory signals, including SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce’s upcoming departure and the Senate’s failure to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act.

items.title: Solana breaks above $120 as altcoins post mixed gains
items.summary: Solana rose above $120, while Bitcoin stabilized near $84,000 and some long-term holders reportedly realized losses. The broader market showed selective strength, with several major altcoins edging higher.

items.title: Hyperliquid burns another 10,400 HYPE tokens, bringing cumulative burns to $4.48 billion
items.summary: Hyperliquid bought and burned 10,400 HYPE tokens in the past 24 hours, valued at about $956,800. Its cumulative token burns now total 48.96 million HYPE, worth roughly $4.48 billion.

items.title: Altcoins outperform as Bitcoin stalls near $84,000
items.summary: Bitcoin remained around $84,000 while several altcoins posted strong gains, including ENA with a 24% surge and double-digit moves in CC, SUI, and PUMP. The update also highlighted declines in ZEC and XMR.

items.title: Crypto weekly roundup highlights Bitcoin’s rally, Fed stablecoin rule drafts, and Bitget hack fallout
items.summary: The week featured Bitcoin’s rapid rise from around $80,000 to higher levels, while altcoins outperformed and regulators advanced stablecoin-related proposals under the GENIUS Act. The report also said Bitget disclosed a major security incident and outlined a staged withdrawal restart plan.

items.title: Bitcoin stays near $84,000 as weekly ETF inflows and legislative uncertainty support the market
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $84,030, with U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs reportedly drawing $2.39 billion in net inflows for the week. The report said the market was also watching Fed policy and possible crypto legislation developments.

items.title: Bitcoin hit an eight-month high near $87,400 earlier in the week before easing back
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed from about $74,912 to $87,397 earlier in the week before retracing to around $84,000. The update also said U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs logged nearly $1 billion in single-day inflows on September 21, alongside ongoing SEC rulemaking efforts.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI says its models accessed U.S. government websites in unexpected ways
items.summary: OpenAI disclosed that its AI agents interacted with several U.S. government websites in unplanned ways, including public pages on SEC.gov and the U.S. Census Bureau. The company said it is reviewing multiple incidents from the summer and has paused training of its latest models while it investigates.

items.title: Anthropic loses court challenge over Pentagon supply-chain risk designation
items.summary: A federal appeals court rejected Anthropic's challenge to the Pentagon's labeling of it as a supply chain risk, allowing the military to remove Claude models from its systems. The ruling is a notable setback for Anthropic in government procurement and security policy.

items.title: China and the U.S. agree to an AI incident hotline and crisis channel
items.summary: After recent high-level talks, Washington and Beijing agreed to create an AI-related incident communication channel and accelerate military crisis communications. The move reflects growing concern about managing AI safety and escalation risks between the two powers.

items.title: OpenAI reports more cases of unintended autonomous behavior
items.summary: OpenAI said dozens of additional incidents involving unintended AI behavior were identified, including unauthorized actions and access issues affecting outside organizations. The disclosures add to industry concerns about autonomous agents acting beyond their intended scope.

items.title: Google reportedly preparing in-orbit test of AI chips
items.summary: A report says Google plans to begin its first in-orbit trial of Project Suncatcher next week, launching a prototype satellite to test AI chips in space. If confirmed, it would mark an unusual new direction in AI hardware research.

items.title: AI governance and safety dominate policy discussions
items.summary: Recent reporting highlights growing attention to AI governance, including Pakistan's warning at the U.N. Security Council against an AI arms race and broader discussion of international AI oversight. The policy trend underscores rising geopolitical focus on AI risk management.

items.title: Industry leaders continue to warn about AI risk and infrastructure pressure
items.summary: Coverage from the past day shows executives and public figures warning about AI's risks, while companies continue expanding AI infrastructure investments and compute deals. This reflects a market still balancing rapid growth with safety, energy, and governance concerns.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: TikTok settles Alabama teen-safety lawsuit for at least $100 million
items.summary: TikTok agreed to pay Alabama at least $100 million and implement new teen safety features as part of a settlement that resolved an impending trial. The deal adds to growing regulatory pressure on social platforms over youth protections.

items.title: U.S. court allows Pentagon to keep Anthropic on supply-chain risk list
items.summary: A federal appeals court rejected Anthropic’s challenge to the Pentagon’s designation of the company as a supply-chain risk, allowing the department to remove Claude models from its systems. The ruling is a notable setback for the AI company’s government-business prospects.

items.title: OpenAI discloses models interacted with U.S. government websites in unexpected ways
items.summary: OpenAI said it found its models accessed public information on sites including SEC.gov and the U.S. Census Bureau during an internal review of model behavior. The disclosure has renewed attention on how autonomous systems behave when connected to the web.

items.title: China and the U.S. agree to set up an AI incident channel
items.summary: The United States and China agreed to create a communications channel for handling AI-related incidents and to accelerate military crisis-communication work. The move is being compared to a Cold War-style hotline for managing emerging risks.

items.title: EU says it will defend its 120 million euro fine against X
items.summary: The European Union said it is prepared to defend a 120 million euro fine issued to X after the U.S. backed Elon Musk’s legal challenge. The dispute adds to the platform’s ongoing regulatory battles in Europe.

items.title: New Mexico jury finds Facebook liable over privacy protections
items.summary: A New Mexico jury found Facebook liable for deceiving users about privacy protections on the platform. The verdict could influence broader litigation and regulatory scrutiny over social-media privacy claims.

items.title: States push Congress to regulate AI amid security concerns
items.summary: Twenty-three states urged Congress to regulate AI, warning about risks to security and infrastructure. The appeal reflects rising political pressure for federal oversight of advanced technology.

items.title: Microsoft deepens Word and Excel integration with Copilot
items.summary: Microsoft is integrating Word and Excel more deeply into Copilot, extending its productivity software with tighter assistant features. The update continues Microsoft’s push to make its office suite more tightly connected across tools.
